summary: The root صمم (Smm) primarily conveys the idea of being deaf or having a blocked ear. It also extends to meaning firmness, resolution, or being determined, as if one is deaf to distractions.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: صّمَّ, (S, M, Msb, K,) and صَمِمَ, which is extr., (M, K,) [first pers. of each صَمِمْتُ,] aor. يَصَمُّ, (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. صَمَمٌ (S, * M, Msb, K) and صَمٌّ; (M, K;) and; (S, M, Msb, K;) He was, or became, deaf; (M, * Msb, K; *) [or] he had a stoppage of the ear, and a heaviness of hearing. (M, K.) And صَمَّتِ الأُ ُنُ, aor. as above, inf. n. صَمَمٌ, The ear was, or became, deaf. (Msb.) [And He was, or became, as though he heard not.

صمّم, said of a sword, (S, M, K, TA,) accord. to the K, signifies It struck the joint, and cut, or severed, it: or i. q. طَبَّقَ: but this is at variance with what is said by J and other leading authorities; which is as follows: (TA:) it penetrated into the bone, and cut, or severed, it; but when it strikes the joint, and cuts, or severs, it, one says طَبَّقَ; a poet says, describing a sword, يُصَمِّمُ أَحْيَانًا وَحِينًا يُطَبِّقُ [ It penetrates into the bone, &c., sometimes, and at one time…

اصمّ, intrans.: see 1, first and fourth sentences. اصمّهُ He, (God, S, Msb, K,) or it, (a disease, M,) rendered him deaf; (S, * M, * Msb, K; *) [or] caused him to have a stoppage of the ear, and a heaviness of hearing. (M, K.) [Hence,] أَصَمَّنِى الكَلَامَ (assumed tropical:) He, or it, diverted me from hearing the speech; as though he, or it, rendered me deaf. (TA.) [Hence, اصمّهُ signifies also (assumed tropical:) He, or it, caused him to be as though he heard not.

تصامّ He feigned himself to be أَصَمّ [i. e. deaf ]. (S.) [It is intrans. and trans.] You say, تصامّ عَنْهُ and تصامّهُ He feigned to him that he was deaf. (M.) And تصامّ عَنِ الحَدِيثِ (M, K) and تصامّهُ (M) He feigned (M, K) to his companion (M) that he was deaf to the narrative, or story. (M, K. *) تَصَامَمْتُهُ means تَصَامَمْتُ مِنْهُ [or عَنْهُ ], i. e. I made a show of being deaf [ to it ], and feigned myself inattentive [ to it ]. (Ham p. 169.)
R. Q. 1 صَمْصَمَ: see 2, in two places. صَمْصَمَتِ الصِّمَّةُ, (TK,) inf. n. صَمْصَمَةٌ, (K, TK,) The female hedge-hog uttered its cry. (K, * TK.)

الصِّمُّ a name for (assumed tropical:) Calamity, or misfortune; (S, TA;) as also, (TA,) and so, like قَطَامِ, in a phrase mentioned in the first paragraph, q. v. (S, K. [See also this last word below.]) And (assumed tropical:) The lion; (S, M, K;) as also, (M, Msb, K,) thus called because of his courage, [i. e. from the latter word as signifying “ courageous, ” but accord. to the Msb the reverse is the case,] (M,) and so and: (K:) the pl. of is صِمَمٌ. (TA.)

صِمَّةٌ Courageous; (S, M, Msb, K;) applied to a man; (S, M;) one who renders deaf him whom he smites. (Er-Rághib, TA.) See also the next preceding paragraph, in three places. Also A male serpent: (S, K:) pl. صِمَمٌ. (S.) And A female hedge-hog. (K.) See also صَمَامٌ.
صَمَمٌ inf. n. of the intrans. verb صَمَّ [q. v.]. (S, * M, Msb, K.) See also صِمْصِمٌ, in four places.

صَمَامِ [an imperative verbal noun, like نَزَالِ &c.]. One says, صَمَامِ صَمَامِ, meaning Feign ye deafness, in silence. (S, K.) Also meaning Charge ye upon the enemy. (AHeyth, TA.) Also (tropical:) Hard, or severe, calamity or misfortune; and so; (K, TA;) [ as though ] closed up [or obdurate, or deaf to deprecation ]: (TA:) or الصَّمَّآءُ signifies [simply] calamity, or misfortune: (S:) and دَاهِيَةٌ signifies a calamity, or misfortune, [ as though ] closed up, and hard.

صِمَامٌ The سِدَاد [or stopper ], (S, M, K,) [i. e.] the thing that is put into the mouth, (Msb,) of a flask, or bottle: (S, M, Msb, K:) and its شِدَاد [app. meaning the piece of skin that is tied over the head ]: (M:) or accord.

صَمِيمٌ The bone that is the [ main ] stay, or support, of the limb or member or the like; (M, K, and Ham p. 302;) as the صميم [or principal bone] of the shank (M and Ham) of a beast, (M,) and that of the head; (M and Ham;) opposed to وَشِيظٌ, because the latter is smaller than the former: (M:) and the thing that is the [ main ] stay, or support, of another thing. (Ham p. 359.) [Hence,] The heart: so in a saying of a poet cited voce دَلَفَ. (Ham p.

صَمَّانٌ Hard ground, (M,) [i. e.] any such ground, (K,) containing stones, by the side of sands; as also: (M, K:) or the latter is a n. un.; and the former signifies hard ground: (Ham p. 285:) or rugged ground, (S, M,) falling short of what is called جَبَلٌ: (M:) it is so called because of its hardness. (TA.)
صَمَّانَةٌ: see the next preceding paragraph.
صَمْصَمٌ Very niggardly or tenacious: (K:) or niggardly, or tenacious, in the utmost degree. (IAar, TA.) See also the next paragraph. [And see ضَمْضَمٌ.]

صِمْصِمٌ, (S, M, K,) applied to a man, (S, M,) Thick: (A'Obeyd, S:) or short and thick: (M, K:) or it signifies, (S,) or signifies also, (K,) bold, or daring; that acts, or proceeds, with penetrative energy, or with sharpness, vigorousness, and effectiveness: (S, K:) and applied to a man and to a horse, (M, K,) and to a mare, (M,) [in like manner,] i. q. [and مُصَمِّمَةٌ (in the CK مُصَمَّمٌ is erroneously put for مُصَمِّمٌ ) i. e.
صُمَصِمٌ: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places: and see also الصِّمُّ.
صَمْصَمَةٌ inf. n. of R. Q. 1 [q. v.] See also the paragraph here following.

صِمْصِمَةٌ A company, or collection, (M, K,) of men; like زِمْزِمَةٌ; neither of which words is formed by substitution from the other: (M, TA: [in the TA in art. زم, this is said of زِمْزِمَةٌ and ضِمْضِمَةٌ:]) pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.]. (M, K.) Also The middle of a people or party; and so. (K.) And A rugged [ hill such as is termed ] أَكَمَة, of which the stones are almost erect. (En-Nadr, TA.)

صَمْصَامٌ, (S, K,) or سَيْفٌ صَمْصَامٌ, (M,) and, (S, M, K, [in the CK, erroneously, صِمْصَامَة,]) A sword, (K,) or a sharp sword, (S, M,) that will not bend. (S, M, K.) الصَّمْصَامُ, (S, K,) or, (M,) was the name of The sword of 'Amr Ibn-Maadee-Kerib. (S, M, K.) And some of the Arabs make, thus without tenween, imperfectly decl., to be the name of A particular sword. (IB, TA.) See also صِمْصِمٌ.
صَمْصَامَةٌ: see the next preceding paragraph, in three places: and see also صِمْصِمٌ.
صُمَاصِمٌ: see صِمْصِمٌ: and see also الصِّمُّ.
صُمَاصِمَةٌ: see صِمْصِمٌ.

أَصَمُّ applied to any animal, (Mgh,) Deaf; (S, * M, * Mgh, Msb, K; *) [or] having a stoppage of the ear, and a heaviness of hearing; (M, K:) fem. صَمَّآءُ: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. صُمٌّ (M, Msb, K) and صُمَّانٌ. (M, K.) A poet says, أَصَمُّ عَمَّا سَآءَهُ سَمِيعُ (TA,) a prov., (Meyd,) meaning Feigning himself deaf to that which displeases him, (Meyd, TA,) i. e. to what is foul, (Meyd,) as though he heard it not, (TA,) but hearing (Meyd, TA) that which pleases him, i. e.
صَوْتٌ مَصِمٌّ A sound, or noise, or voice, that deafens the ear-hole. (TA.)
أَلْفٌ مُصَمَّمٌ (assumed tropical:) A thousand completed; like مُصَمَّتٌ and مُصْمَتٌ. (TA in art. صمت.)

مُصَمِّمٌ A sword that passes into the bones: (M:) or that penetrates into that which is struck with it. (TA.) See also صِمْصِمٌ. And (assumed tropical:) A strong camel: so says Aboo-' Amr Esh-Sheybánee: and he cites the saying, حَمَّلْتُ أَثْقَالِى مُصَمِّمَاتِهَا [as meaning I loaded their strong camels with my burdens ]: (TA:) or the مُصَمِّمَات, here mentioned, are the camels that do not utter a grumbling cry; patient of travel. (Ham p. 791.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
